title: Backups Aren't Simple
title_zh: 备份系统不是简单的任务

paragraphs.en: See also: John Salvatier’s excellent blog, Reality has a surprising amount of detail
paragraphs.zh: 另请参阅：John Salvatier 的优秀博客《Reality has a surprising amount of detail》（现实拥有惊人的细节量）

paragraphs.en: I read a comment somewhere that stuck with me, that went something like this:
paragraphs.zh: 我曾在某处读到过一条让我印象深刻的评论，大意是这样的：

paragraphs.en: “There are two types of people: those who have suffered a catastrophic loss of data, and those who will.”
paragraphs.zh: “世上有两种人：一种是已经遭受过灾难性数据丢失的人，另一种是即将遭受的人。”

paragraphs.en: Trying to find the source for it for this blog, it turned out that every other sysadmin has his rehashed version of the quote, but the gist of it is the same everywhere. Data loss is something that happens more often than we’d hope, and most of us are woefully unprepared for when it hits us (which is almost always at the worst possible time).
paragraphs.zh: 为了写这篇博客，我试图找出这句话的出处，结果发现几乎每个系统管理员都有自己的翻版说法，但大意到处都是一样的。 数据丢失的发生频率比我们希望的更高，而我们大多数人对此毫无准备，一旦遇上就束手无策（而且它几乎总是发生在最糟糕的时刻）。

sents.en: Trying to find the source for it for this blog, it turned out that every other sysadmin has his rehashed version of the quote, but the gist of it is the same everywhere.
sents.zh: 为了写这篇博客，我试图找出这句话的出处，结果发现几乎每个系统管理员都有自己的翻版说法，但大意到处都是一样的。

sents.en: Data loss is something that happens more often than we’d hope, and most of us are woefully unprepared for when it hits us (which is almost always at the worst possible time).
sents.zh: 数据丢失的发生频率比我们希望的更高，而我们大多数人对此毫无准备，一旦遇上就束手无策（而且它几乎总是发生在最糟糕的时刻）。

paragraphs.en: I can confirm that I had a similar experience once. When I was little we had pulled all our family photos from our home laptops and PCs onto an external hard drive, in order to free up some space. This worked beautifully until one day my dad wanted to use the drive as storage for our TV set-top box (one of these old things ), and was prompted to format the drive. He went ahead with it, and the disk was reformatted. The index of files was deleted, and we were stuck with a nominally empty drive.
paragraphs.zh: 我可以确认我也曾有过一次类似的经历。 我小时候，我们曾把家里所有笔记本电脑和台式机上的家庭照片都转移到一个外置硬盘上，以便腾出一些空间。 这一直运作良好，直到有一天我爸想把这个硬盘当作我们电视机顶盒的存储设备（就是那种老式的东西之一），然后被提示要格式化硬盘。 他继续操作了，磁盘就被重新格式化了。 文件索引被删除了，我们只能面对一个名义上是空的硬盘。

sents.en: I can confirm that I had a similar experience once.
sents.zh: 我可以确认我也曾有过一次类似的经历。

sents.en: When I was little we had pulled all our family photos from our home laptops and PCs onto an external hard drive, in order to free up some space.
sents.zh: 我小时候，我们曾把家里所有笔记本电脑和台式机上的家庭照片都转移到一个外置硬盘上，以便腾出一些空间。

sents.en: This worked beautifully until one day my dad wanted to use the drive as storage for our TV set-top box (one of these old things ), and was prompted to format the drive.
sents.zh: 这一直运作良好，直到有一天我爸想把这个硬盘当作我们电视机顶盒的存储设备（就是那种老式的东西之一），然后被提示要格式化硬盘。

sents.en: He went ahead with it, and the disk was reformatted.
sents.zh: 他继续操作了，磁盘就被重新格式化了。

sents.en: The index of files was deleted, and we were stuck with a nominally empty drive.
sents.zh: 文件索引被删除了，我们只能面对一个名义上是空的硬盘。

paragraphs.en: It would be easy to blame him for screwing up, but it takes beginning a career in tech to realise that there is a series of errors that lead to this kind of mistake. Firstly, we had put all of our photos in one place and didn’t bother with backups. Secondly, most consumer-facing software usually has bold disclaimers telling you that formatting a disk means losing data (which the set-top box didn’t, terrible UI). Besides, why would you even expect a non-technical person to even have to know any of this?
paragraphs.zh: 把责任都推到他身上很容易，但只有开始了科技行业的职业生涯，才会意识到导致这类错误的是一连串的失误。 首先，我们把所有照片都放在一个地方，也没有费心做备份。 其次，大多数面向消费者的软件通常会有醒目的免责声明，告诉你格式化磁盘意味着数据丢失（而那台机顶盒却没有，糟糕的用户界面）。 再说，凭什么指望一个非技术人员非得知道这些呢？

sents.en: It would be easy to blame him for screwing up, but it takes beginning a career in tech to realise that there is a series of errors that lead to this kind of mistake.
sents.zh: 把责任都推到他身上很容易，但只有开始了科技行业的职业生涯，才会意识到导致这类错误的是一连串的失误。

sents.en: Firstly, we had put all of our photos in one place and didn’t bother with backups.
sents.zh: 首先，我们把所有照片都放在一个地方，也没有费心做备份。

sents.en: Secondly, most consumer-facing software usually has bold disclaimers telling you that formatting a disk means losing data (which the set-top box didn’t, terrible UI).
sents.zh: 其次，大多数面向消费者的软件通常会有醒目的免责声明，告诉你格式化磁盘意味着数据丢失（而那台机顶盒却没有，糟糕的用户界面）。

sents.en: Besides, why would you even expect a non-technical person to even have to know any of this?
sents.zh: 再说，凭什么指望一个非技术人员非得知道这些呢？

paragraphs.en: Thankfully we were able to get the photos restored, and it turned out to be a cheap lesson in handling data. You never keep important things in one place only. There’s about a million things that can go wrong. Your drive could die, it could be stolen, bits could rot in cold storage (hard drives have magnetic particles which can inexplicably shift, and SSDs are made of NAND transistors which leak electricity and over time, corrupt your data).
paragraphs.zh: 谢天谢地，我们最终成功恢复了照片，而这算是处理数据方面一个代价低廉的教训。 重要的事情绝不能只放在一个地方。 可能出问题的事情大约有上百万种。 你的硬盘可能会损坏，可能会被偷，数据位在冷存储中可能会腐烂（硬盘含有磁性颗粒，它们会莫名地发生位移；固态硬盘由 NAND 晶体管构成，会漏电，久而久之会损坏你的数据）。

sents.en: Thankfully we were able to get the photos restored, and it turned out to be a cheap lesson in handling data.
sents.zh: 谢天谢地，我们最终成功恢复了照片，而这算是处理数据方面一个代价低廉的教训。

sents.en: You never keep important things in one place only.
sents.zh: 重要的事情绝不能只放在一个地方。

sents.en: There’s about a million things that can go wrong.
sents.zh: 可能出问题的事情大约有上百万种。

sents.en: Your drive could die, it could be stolen, bits could rot in cold storage (hard drives have magnetic particles which can inexplicably shift, and SSDs are made of NAND transistors which leak electricity and over time, corrupt your data).
sents.zh: 你的硬盘可能会损坏，可能会被偷，数据位在冷存储中可能会腐烂（硬盘含有磁性颗粒，它们会莫名地发生位移；固态硬盘由 NAND 晶体管构成，会漏电，久而久之会损坏你的数据）。

paragraphs.en: So our first principle is to have a backup , i.e. a copy of your files someplace else. So far so good.
paragraphs.zh: 所以我们的第一原则是要有一个备份，也就是把你的文件副本存放在其他地方。到目前为止一切顺利。

paragraphs.en: This doesn’t cover the headaches of what a plugged in drive could do. Ransomware could encrypt your files, and you could do anything from an honest mistake like deleting the wrong file; up to catastrophic mistakes like running a script that overwrites everything with zeroes.
paragraphs.zh: 这并未涵盖已接入的驱动器可能带来的种种麻烦。 勒索软件可能加密你的文件，而且你可能犯各种错误，从误删错误文件这类无心之失，到运行一个用零覆盖所有数据的脚本这类灾难性错误，不一而足。

sents.en: This doesn’t cover the headaches of what a plugged in drive could do.
sents.zh: 这并未涵盖已接入的驱动器可能带来的种种麻烦。

sents.en: Ransomware could encrypt your files, and you could do anything from an honest mistake like deleting the wrong file; up to catastrophic mistakes like running a script that overwrites everything with zeroes.
sents.zh: 勒索软件可能加密你的文件，而且你可能犯各种错误，从误删错误文件这类无心之失，到运行一个用零覆盖所有数据的脚本这类灾难性错误，不一而足。

paragraphs.en: So our backup should not be a mirror of the first drive, because we also want to be able to go back in time if we mess up. Importantly, this means that mirroring your disk with something like RAID 1 is out. We need some other method that snapshots things.
paragraphs.zh: 所以我们的备份不应该是第一块硬盘的镜像，因为当我们搞砸了的时候，还需要能够回到过去。 重要的是，这意味着像 RAID 1 那样对磁盘做镜像的方式就行不通了。 我们需要某种能对内容做快照的其他方法。

sents.en: So our backup should not be a mirror of the first drive, because we also want to be able to go back in time if we mess up.
sents.zh: 所以我们的备份不应该是第一块硬盘的镜像，因为当我们搞砸了的时候，还需要能够回到过去。

sents.en: Importantly, this means that mirroring your disk with something like RAID 1 is out.
sents.zh: 重要的是，这意味着像 RAID 1 那样对磁盘做镜像的方式就行不通了。

sents.en: We need some other method that snapshots things.
sents.zh: 我们需要某种能对内容做快照的其他方法。

paragraphs.en: How often do we want to take snapshots? Maybe in our case with the photos we should have run a backup every week. If we lose 6 days and 23 hours of data, that’s fine and we can live with it. This is what’s called a Recovery Point Objective (RPO) in IT, and in real cases, it ranges from <30 seconds for critical financial institutions which really can’t afford to lose data, to 24 hours or more for some small enterprises (if they even have a disaster recovery strategy).
paragraphs.zh: 我们想要多久拍摄一次快照？ 也许在我们的照片场景中，我们应该每周运行一次备份。 如果我们丢失了 6 天 23 小时的数据，那也没问题，我们可以接受。 这就是 IT 领域所说的恢复点目标（RPO），在实际情况中，它的范围从关键金融机构的不到 30 秒（它们真的承受不起数据丢失），到一些小型企业的 24 小时甚至更长（如果它们有灾难恢复策略的话）。

sents.en: How often do we want to take snapshots?
sents.zh: 我们想要多久拍摄一次快照？

sents.en: Maybe in our case with the photos we should have run a backup every week.
sents.zh: 也许在我们的照片场景中，我们应该每周运行一次备份。

sents.en: If we lose 6 days and 23 hours of data, that’s fine and we can live with it.
sents.zh: 如果我们丢失了 6 天 23 小时的数据，那也没问题，我们可以接受。

sents.en: This is what’s called a Recovery Point Objective (RPO) in IT, and in real cases, it ranges from <30 seconds for critical financial institutions which really can’t afford to lose data, to 24 hours or more for some small enterprises (if they even have a disaster recovery strategy).
sents.zh: 这就是 IT 领域所说的恢复点目标（RPO），在实际情况中，它的范围从关键金融机构的不到 30 秒（它们真的承受不起数据丢失），到一些小型企业的 24 小时甚至更长（如果它们有灾难恢复策略的话）。

paragraphs.en: Taking snapshots means that we have an increasing burden on our storage. With an RPO of 24 hours, you will end up having 7 snapshots per week. 30 per month. 365 per year, if you really don’t go and prune your snapshots. So you need to rotate your backups .
paragraphs.zh: 制作快照意味着我们的存储负担会不断增加。 如果 RPO 为 24 小时，而你真的不去清理快照，那么最终每周会有 7 个快照，每月 30 个，每年 365 个。 因此你需要轮换你的备份。

sents.en: Taking snapshots means that we have an increasing burden on our storage.
sents.zh: 制作快照意味着我们的存储负担会不断增加。

sents.en: With an RPO of 24 hours, you will end up having 7 snapshots per week. 30 per month. 365 per year, if you really don’t go and prune your snapshots.
sents.zh: 如果 RPO 为 24 小时，而你真的不去清理快照，那么最终每周会有 7 个快照，每月 30 个，每年 365 个。

sents.en: So you need to rotate your backups .
sents.zh: 因此你需要轮换你的备份。

paragraphs.en: Let’s say I go with the naive approach and decide to keep 14 days’ worth of snapshots. When I take a new snapshot, I delete the oldest one and I add the new one. Pretty simple, but this now forces me to have a watchful eye. Maybe I keep lots of data and can’t be bothered to check if something got corrupted in the past two weeks? But then again, I can’t just store a year’s worth of backups and they’re simply not relevant to me. What happened between day 2 and day 3 of the year has almost no significance when it’s day 364. So the granularity at which we take backups must change. The closer we are to today, the more frequent the snapshots. The further back, the less frequent the snapshots.
paragraphs.zh: 假设我采用最简单的方法，决定保留 14 天的快照。 当我拍摄新快照时，就删除最旧的一个，再添加新的。 很简单，但这迫使我要时刻保持警惕。 也许我保留了大量数据，懒得去检查过去两周里是否有东西损坏了？ 但话说回来，我也不能存储一整年的备份，因为它们对我而言根本不相关。 当已经是第 364 天时，一年中第 2 天和第 3 天之间发生了什么几乎没有意义。 所以我们进行备份的粒度必须改变。 离今天越近，快照的频率就越高。 往前追溯越远，快照的频率就越低。

sents.en: Let’s say I go with the naive approach and decide to keep 14 days’ worth of snapshots.
sents.zh: 假设我采用最简单的方法，决定保留 14 天的快照。

sents.en: When I take a new snapshot, I delete the oldest one and I add the new one.
sents.zh: 当我拍摄新快照时，就删除最旧的一个，再添加新的。

sents.en: Pretty simple, but this now forces me to have a watchful eye.
sents.zh: 很简单，但这迫使我要时刻保持警惕。

sents.en: Maybe I keep lots of data and can’t be bothered to check if something got corrupted in the past two weeks?
sents.zh: 也许我保留了大量数据，懒得去检查过去两周里是否有东西损坏了？

sents.en: But then again, I can’t just store a year’s worth of backups and they’re simply not relevant to me.
sents.zh: 但话说回来，我也不能存储一整年的备份，因为它们对我而言根本不相关。

sents.en: What happened between day 2 and day 3 of the year has almost no significance when it’s day 364.
sents.zh: 当已经是第 364 天时，一年中第 2 天和第 3 天之间发生了什么几乎没有意义。

sents.en: So the granularity at which we take backups must change.
sents.zh: 所以我们进行备份的粒度必须改变。

sents.en: The closer we are to today, the more frequent the snapshots.
sents.zh: 离今天越近，快照的频率就越高。

sents.en: The further back, the less frequent the snapshots.
sents.zh: 往前追溯越远，快照的频率就越低。

paragraphs.en: So maybe we rotate our daily backups every 14 days, but also take weekly backups that we rotate every 7 weeks, and monthly backups we rotate every 12 months. This should be much more efficient. But again our complexity grows. We now have something called a GFS-rotated, snapshot-based backup . This list of adjectives will continue growing, as we’ll see in a bit.
paragraphs.zh: 因此，也许我们把每日备份每 14 天轮换一次，但同时也进行每周备份并每 7 周轮换一次，还有每月备份每 12 个月轮换一次。 这样应该会高效得多。 但同样，我们的复杂度也在增长。 现在我们有了一种叫做 GFS 轮换、基于快照的备份。 正如我们稍后会看到的，这一长串形容词还会继续增加。

sents.en: So maybe we rotate our daily backups every 14 days, but also take weekly backups that we rotate every 7 weeks, and monthly backups we rotate every 12 months.
sents.zh: 因此，也许我们把每日备份每 14 天轮换一次，但同时也进行每周备份并每 7 周轮换一次，还有每月备份每 12 个月轮换一次。

sents.en: This should be much more efficient.
sents.zh: 这样应该会高效得多。

sents.en: But again our complexity grows.
sents.zh: 但同样，我们的复杂度也在增长。

sents.en: We now have something called a GFS-rotated, snapshot-based backup .
sents.zh: 现在我们有了一种叫做 GFS 轮换、基于快照的备份。

sents.en: This list of adjectives will continue growing, as we’ll see in a bit.
sents.zh: 正如我们稍后会看到的，这一长串形容词还会继续增加。

paragraphs.en: Maybe then you take a look at how MPEG compresses video , and get fascinated by how a calm scene in a movie, where the protagonist speaks but otherwise doesn’t move against a completely still background can be used for compressing video. You notice that videos are composed of frames that are mostly similar to each other, only changing with a certain movement that can be represented as a vector for a fraction of the storage. Which leads you to the very logical conclusion that your snapshots also follow the same pattern! Even more, it turns out that file changes follow a fat-tailed distribution, so over a given period there are a vast majority of files that don’t get changed at all, and a very tiny minority that change all the time.
paragraphs.zh: 也许接下来你会看看 MPEG 是如何压缩视频的，并被电影中一个平静场景的压缩方式所吸引：主角在说话，但除此之外没有动作，背景也完全静止，这样的画面可以用来压缩视频。 你注意到视频由彼此大多相似的帧组成，只有在发生某种移动时才变化，而这种移动可以表示为一个向量，只需占用一小部分存储空间。 由此你得出一个非常合乎逻辑的结论：你的快照也遵循同样的模式！ 更进一步，事实证明文件的变化遵循厚尾分布，因此在给定的时间段内，绝大多数文件完全不会被改动，而只有极少数文件会不停地变化。

sents.en: Maybe then you take a look at how MPEG compresses video , and get fascinated by how a calm scene in a movie, where the protagonist speaks but otherwise doesn’t move against a completely still background can be used for compressing video.
sents.zh: 也许接下来你会看看 MPEG 是如何压缩视频的，并被电影中一个平静场景的压缩方式所吸引：主角在说话，但除此之外没有动作，背景也完全静止，这样的画面可以用来压缩视频。

sents.en: You notice that videos are composed of frames that are mostly similar to each other, only changing with a certain movement that can be represented as a vector for a fraction of the storage.
sents.zh: 你注意到视频由彼此大多相似的帧组成，只有在发生某种移动时才变化，而这种移动可以表示为一个向量，只需占用一小部分存储空间。

sents.en: Which leads you to the very logical conclusion that your snapshots also follow the same pattern!
sents.zh: 由此你得出一个非常合乎逻辑的结论：你的快照也遵循同样的模式！

sents.en: Even more, it turns out that file changes follow a fat-tailed distribution, so over a given period there are a vast majority of files that don’t get changed at all, and a very tiny minority that change all the time.
sents.zh: 更进一步，事实证明文件的变化遵循厚尾分布，因此在给定的时间段内，绝大多数文件完全不会被改动，而只有极少数文件会不停地变化。

paragraphs.en: So it becomes obvious that we shouldn’t store identical copies of files, but rather deduplicate . We can use hard links when we need to reference an already existing file. This way, we store one file on disk, and then reference it from each of our snapshots. This also survives backup rotation because we never delete files, we only delete directory entries. This exact approach is used by rsnapshot , and is best described as an incremental backup, because we store only the changes between two adjacent snapshots, instead of all the changes since the latest full backup (these are called differential backups and are more robust when restoring, but I won’t get into it for the sake of brevity).
paragraphs.zh: 因此很明显，我们不应该存储完全相同的文件副本，而应该进行去重。 当需要引用一个已存在的文件时，我们可以使用硬链接。 这样，我们在磁盘上只存储一个文件，然后在每个快照中引用它。 这种方式在备份轮换时依然有效，因为我们从不删除文件，只删除目录项。 rsnapshot 使用的正是这种方法，最好将其描述为增量备份，因为我们只存储两个相邻快照之间的变化，而不是自最近一次完整备份以来的所有变化（后者称为差异备份，在恢复时更可靠，但为简洁起见，我不展开讨论）。

sents.en: So it becomes obvious that we shouldn’t store identical copies of files, but rather deduplicate .
sents.zh: 因此很明显，我们不应该存储完全相同的文件副本，而应该进行去重。

sents.en: We can use hard links when we need to reference an already existing file.
sents.zh: 当需要引用一个已存在的文件时，我们可以使用硬链接。

sents.en: This way, we store one file on disk, and then reference it from each of our snapshots.
sents.zh: 这样，我们在磁盘上只存储一个文件，然后在每个快照中引用它。

sents.en: This also survives backup rotation because we never delete files, we only delete directory entries.
sents.zh: 这种方式在备份轮换时依然有效，因为我们从不删除文件，只删除目录项。

sents.en: This exact approach is used by rsnapshot , and is best described as an incremental backup, because we store only the changes between two adjacent snapshots, instead of all the changes since the latest full backup (these are called differential backups and are more robust when restoring, but I won’t get into it for the sake of brevity).
sents.zh: rsnapshot 使用的正是这种方法，最好将其描述为增量备份，因为我们只存储两个相邻快照之间的变化，而不是自最近一次完整备份以来的所有变化（后者称为差异备份，在恢复时更可靠，但为简洁起见，我不展开讨论）。

paragraphs.en: The savings in storage are not the only benefit we get from doing this. We briefly mentioned in the beginning that we don’t store everything on a single machine. Obviously, there is also networking involved in this process, since we need to actually transfer the files from one machine to another. Deduplicated backups save a lot of bandwidth, which is especially important if you use a cloud service as your second machine. It directly affects you financially.
paragraphs.zh: 这样做带来的节省存储空间并不是我们获得的唯一好处。 我们在开头简要提到过，我们不会把所有东西都存储在一台机器上。 显然，这个过程中还涉及网络传输，因为我们需要真正地把文件从一台机器传到另一台机器。 去重后的备份可以节省大量带宽，如果你使用云服务作为第二台机器，这一点尤其重要。 它会直接影响到你的经济支出。

sents.en: The savings in storage are not the only benefit we get from doing this.
sents.zh: 这样做带来的节省存储空间并不是我们获得的唯一好处。

sents.en: We briefly mentioned in the beginning that we don’t store everything on a single machine.
sents.zh: 我们在开头简要提到过，我们不会把所有东西都存储在一台机器上。

sents.en: Obviously, there is also networking involved in this process, since we need to actually transfer the files from one machine to another.
sents.zh: 显然，这个过程中还涉及网络传输，因为我们需要真正地把文件从一台机器传到另一台机器。

sents.en: Deduplicated backups save a lot of bandwidth, which is especially important if you use a cloud service as your second machine.
sents.zh: 去重后的备份可以节省大量带宽，如果你使用云服务作为第二台机器，这一点尤其重要。

sents.en: It directly affects you financially.
sents.zh: 它会直接影响到你的经济支出。

paragraphs.en: To sum up, by this time we have created an incremental, deduplicated, GFS-rotated, snapshot-based backup . We can use rsync to pull the files from the main machine, and cronjobs to run our backup scripts. We can run backups on as many machines as we’d like, and adding another one is trivial. Even better, file metadata is preserved, so things like access permissions and file ownership are fine.
paragraphs.zh: 总而言之，到目前为止我们已经创建了一种增量的、去重的、采用 GFS 轮转的、基于快照的备份。 我们可以使用 rsync 从主机拉取文件，并使用 cronjob 来运行备份脚本。 我们可以在任意多的机器上运行备份，而添加另一台机器也非常简单。 更好的是，文件元数据得以保留，因此访问权限和文件所有者等信息都不会有问题。

sents.en: To sum up, by this time we have created an incremental, deduplicated, GFS-rotated, snapshot-based backup .
sents.zh: 总而言之，到目前为止我们已经创建了一种增量的、去重的、采用 GFS 轮转的、基于快照的备份。

sents.en: We can use rsync to pull the files from the main machine, and cronjobs to run our backup scripts.
sents.zh: 我们可以使用 rsync 从主机拉取文件，并使用 cronjob 来运行备份脚本。

sents.en: We can run backups on as many machines as we’d like, and adding another one is trivial.
sents.zh: 我们可以在任意多的机器上运行备份，而添加另一台机器也非常简单。

sents.en: Even better, file metadata is preserved, so things like access permissions and file ownership are fine.
sents.zh: 更好的是，文件元数据得以保留，因此访问权限和文件所有者等信息都不会有问题。

paragraphs.en: Motivated by our success in developing this solution, we try to use it to backup the homelab with its 10 Docker containers. But later we find out from logs on the individual machines that backups are failing. The reason being that many Docker containers like to create root-owned files, and if you’re not careful you can create a cronjob running as the default user.
paragraphs.zh: 受到成功开发该解决方案的鼓舞，我们尝试用它来备份拥有 10 个 Docker 容器的家庭实验室。 但后来我们从各台机器的日志中发现备份失败了。 原因在于许多 Docker 容器喜欢创建属于 root 的文件，而且如果不小心，你可能会创建一个以默认用户身份运行的 cronjob。

sents.en: Motivated by our success in developing this solution, we try to use it to backup the homelab with its 10 Docker containers.
sents.zh: 受到成功开发该解决方案的鼓舞，我们尝试用它来备份拥有 10 个 Docker 容器的家庭实验室。

sents.en: But later we find out from logs on the individual machines that backups are failing.
sents.zh: 但后来我们从各台机器的日志中发现备份失败了。

sents.en: The reason being that many Docker containers like to create root-owned files, and if you’re not careful you can create a cronjob running as the default user.
sents.zh: 原因在于许多 Docker 容器喜欢创建属于 root 的文件，而且如果不小心，你可能会创建一个以默认用户身份运行的 cronjob。

paragraphs.en: To make matters worse, almost every web app uses a database of some kind. Databases sometimes like to store things in-memory and flush them to disk in batches to improve performance. This practically means that restoring from backup will fail due to data corruption if we are unlucky. So we make the backup also dump the databases, and give it full filesystem permissions on our Docker volumes. That should make it work!
paragraphs.zh: 更糟糕的是，几乎所有 Web 应用都会使用某种数据库。 数据库有时会把数据先存放在内存中，再分批刷写到磁盘上，以提升性能。 这实际上意味着，如果运气不好，从备份恢复时会因数据损坏而失败。 因此我们让备份程序同时导出数据库，并在我们的 Docker 卷上授予它完整的文件系统权限。 这样应该就能正常工作了！

sents.en: To make matters worse, almost every web app uses a database of some kind.
sents.zh: 更糟糕的是，几乎所有 Web 应用都会使用某种数据库。

sents.en: Databases sometimes like to store things in-memory and flush them to disk in batches to improve performance.
sents.zh: 数据库有时会把数据先存放在内存中，再分批刷写到磁盘上，以提升性能。

sents.en: This practically means that restoring from backup will fail due to data corruption if we are unlucky.
sents.zh: 这实际上意味着，如果运气不好，从备份恢复时会因数据损坏而失败。

sents.en: So we make the backup also dump the databases, and give it full filesystem permissions on our Docker volumes.
sents.zh: 因此我们让备份程序同时导出数据库，并在我们的 Docker 卷上授予它完整的文件系统权限。

sents.en: That should make it work!
sents.zh: 这样应该就能正常工作了！

paragraphs.en: Then you read about incidents in which a model of hard drive had famously high failure rates, and start to wonder if you should maybe store your backups on two machines with different types of media. That way a hardware-specific failure would be unlikely to wipe out your backups. And while we’re on the topic of physical security, have one offsite backup on the cloud or a machine at a family member’s house. This way you make it really unlikely that a power surge, flood or fire will destroy everything. This is where the 3-2-1 backup gets its name: 3 copies, on 2 different types of media, with 1 offsite.
paragraphs.zh: 然后，你读到一些关于某型号硬盘故障率高得出名的事故报道，开始琢磨是否应该把备份存储在两台使用不同类型介质的机器上。 这样一来，某个特定硬件发生故障就不太可能毁掉你所有的备份。 既然说到物理安全这个话题，可以在云端或亲戚家的机器上保留一份异地备份。 这样一来，电涌、洪水或火灾毁掉一切的可能性就变得非常低。 这就是 3-2-1 备份名称的由来：3 份副本，存储在 2 种不同类型的介质上，并保留 1 份异地备份。

sents.en: Then you read about incidents in which a model of hard drive had famously high failure rates, and start to wonder if you should maybe store your backups on two machines with different types of media.
sents.zh: 然后，你读到一些关于某型号硬盘故障率高得出名的事故报道，开始琢磨是否应该把备份存储在两台使用不同类型介质的机器上。

sents.en: That way a hardware-specific failure would be unlikely to wipe out your backups.
sents.zh: 这样一来，某个特定硬件发生故障就不太可能毁掉你所有的备份。

sents.en: And while we’re on the topic of physical security, have one offsite backup on the cloud or a machine at a family member’s house.
sents.zh: 既然说到物理安全这个话题，可以在云端或亲戚家的机器上保留一份异地备份。

sents.en: This way you make it really unlikely that a power surge, flood or fire will destroy everything.
sents.zh: 这样一来，电涌、洪水或火灾毁掉一切的可能性就变得非常低。

sents.en: This is where the 3-2-1 backup gets its name: 3 copies, on 2 different types of media, with 1 offsite.
sents.zh: 这就是 3-2-1 备份名称的由来：3 份副本，存储在 2 种不同类型的介质上，并保留 1 份异地备份。

paragraphs.en: Let’s say you decide on a cloud provider for your offsite backup. Specifically object storage like Amazon S3. You quickly find out that our current setup won’t work because one, files lose their metadata when you upload them to S3, and two, the price for uploading many small files to S3 is punitively high (file sizes also follow a fat-tailed distribution). These two facts make it best for you to stick many files into a tarball. That way you retain both your file metadata as well as your low costs. But the question is, how do you do that? Do you stick everything in one giant tarball? Obviously not, then your incremental backups with the hard links stop making sense. Best to split everything in clean 50MB chunks, but good luck with doing that in a way that is verifiably safe!
paragraphs.zh: 假设你决定为异地备份选择一家云服务提供商。 具体来说，是像 Amazon S3 那样的对象存储。 你很快就会发现，当前的方案行不通，原因有二：一是文件上传到 S3 后会丢失元数据，二是向 S3 上传大量小文件的费用高得离谱（文件大小同样服从肥尾分布）。 这两个事实意味着，你最好把许多文件打包进一个 tar 包。 这样既能保留文件元数据，又能保持低成本。 但问题来了，该怎么做呢？ 把所有东西塞进一个巨大的 tar 包？ 显然不行，那样的话基于硬链接的增量备份就失去意义了。 最好的做法是把所有内容切分成整齐的 50MB 块，但要想以可验证安全的方式做到这一点，可就难了！

sents.en: Let’s say you decide on a cloud provider for your offsite backup.
sents.zh: 假设你决定为异地备份选择一家云服务提供商。

sents.en: Specifically object storage like Amazon S3.
sents.zh: 具体来说，是像 Amazon S3 那样的对象存储。

sents.en: You quickly find out that our current setup won’t work because one, files lose their metadata when you upload them to S3, and two, the price for uploading many small files to S3 is punitively high (file sizes also follow a fat-tailed distribution).
sents.zh: 你很快就会发现，当前的方案行不通，原因有二：一是文件上传到 S3 后会丢失元数据，二是向 S3 上传大量小文件的费用高得离谱（文件大小同样服从肥尾分布）。

sents.en: These two facts make it best for you to stick many files into a tarball.
sents.zh: 这两个事实意味着，你最好把许多文件打包进一个 tar 包。

sents.en: That way you retain both your file metadata as well as your low costs.
sents.zh: 这样既能保留文件元数据，又能保持低成本。

sents.en: But the question is, how do you do that?
sents.zh: 但问题来了，该怎么做呢？

sents.en: Do you stick everything in one giant tarball?
sents.zh: 把所有东西塞进一个巨大的 tar 包？

sents.en: Obviously not, then your incremental backups with the hard links stop making sense.
sents.zh: 显然不行，那样的话基于硬链接的增量备份就失去意义了。

sents.en: Best to split everything in clean 50MB chunks, but good luck with doing that in a way that is verifiably safe!
sents.zh: 最好的做法是把所有内容切分成整齐的 50MB 块，但要想以可验证安全的方式做到这一点，可就难了！

paragraphs.en: Up until this point, rolling your own backups sounded like something you should be able to do in an afternoon, but this is where I’d give up. It simply isn’t worth the mental load to do all this. Instead, you just use tried and tested tools like Borg or Restic which handle all this and much more (encryption, chunk-level deduplication, checksums). And just give your utmost thanks to the wonderful open-source community for building, maintaining, and live-testing these tools, while respecting how much trial and error was necessary to get to the point where all this complexity is abstracted away for us.
paragraphs.zh: 到目前为止，自己动手做备份听起来像是你一个下午就能搞定的事情，但正是在这里我会选择放弃。 承担这一切带来的心智负担实在不值得。 相反，你只需使用久经考验的工具，比如 Borg 或 Restic，它们能处理所有这些以及更多的事情（加密、分块级去重、校验和）。 并且请向美妙的开源社区致以最诚挚的感谢，感谢他们构建、维护并实际测试这些工具，同时也请体谅，要达到如今这份复杂性为我们抽象掉的境界，需要经历多少反复的试验与失败。

sents.en: Up until this point, rolling your own backups sounded like something you should be able to do in an afternoon, but this is where I’d give up.
sents.zh: 到目前为止，自己动手做备份听起来像是你一个下午就能搞定的事情，但正是在这里我会选择放弃。

sents.en: It simply isn’t worth the mental load to do all this.
sents.zh: 承担这一切带来的心智负担实在不值得。

sents.en: Instead, you just use tried and tested tools like Borg or Restic which handle all this and much more (encryption, chunk-level deduplication, checksums).
sents.zh: 相反，你只需使用久经考验的工具，比如 Borg 或 Restic，它们能处理所有这些以及更多的事情（加密、分块级去重、校验和）。

sents.en: And just give your utmost thanks to the wonderful open-source community for building, maintaining, and live-testing these tools, while respecting how much trial and error was necessary to get to the point where all this complexity is abstracted away for us.
sents.zh: 并且请向美妙的开源社区致以最诚挚的感谢，感谢他们构建、维护并实际测试这些工具，同时也请体谅，要达到如今这份复杂性为我们抽象掉的境界，需要经历多少反复的试验与失败。

paragraphs.en: Obviously, none of this is worth anything if you don’t actually test restores. So that’s also a little digital hygiene article that you will have added to your to-do list. So, as long as you run restores every 6 months, you can enjoy your:
paragraphs.zh: 显然，如果你不真正测试恢复操作，这一切都毫无价值。 所以这也是你将添加到待办清单中的又一项数字卫生事项。 因此，只要你每 6 个月运行一次恢复操作，你就可以尽情享受你的：

sents.en: Obviously, none of this is worth anything if you don’t actually test restores.
sents.zh: 显然，如果你不真正测试恢复操作，这一切都毫无价值。

sents.en: So that’s also a little digital hygiene article that you will have added to your to-do list.
sents.zh: 所以这也是你将添加到待办清单中的又一项数字卫生事项。

sents.en: So, as long as you run restores every 6 months, you can enjoy your:
sents.zh: 因此，只要你每 6 个月运行一次恢复操作，你就可以尽情享受你的：

paragraphs.en: Also make sure not to run backups at 2AM or 3AM, or things may get scary.
paragraphs.zh: 另外，请确保不要在凌晨 2 点或凌晨 3 点运行备份，否则情况可能会变得可怕。

paragraphs.en: A big thank you to everyone for discussing this topic with me. Here are some important things that either slipped my mind, I wasn’t aware of, or otherwise left out of the main article:
paragraphs.zh: 非常感谢大家和我一起讨论这个话题。 以下是一些重要事项，它们要么被我一时间遗忘，要么是我此前并不知晓，或者由于其他原因未写入正文：

sents.en: A big thank you to everyone for discussing this topic with me.
sents.zh: 非常感谢大家和我一起讨论这个话题。

sents.en: Here are some important things that either slipped my mind, I wasn’t aware of, or otherwise left out of the main article:
sents.zh: 以下是一些重要事项，它们要么被我一时间遗忘，要么是我此前并不知晓，或者由于其他原因未写入正文：

paragraphs.en: Consistency groups. The article kinda almost gets there, but stops right before it realizes there’s a problem. If you have multiple programs accessing the storage, s.a. a database (that you are snapshotting) and the application using the database, then you are risking an inconsistent snapshot when the database state you wrote is ahead or behind the application state. You need a mechanism to freeze all I/O beside the snapshot in order to ensure that the snapshot data is useful.
paragraphs.zh: 一致性组。 这篇文章差不多接近要点了，但就在意识到存在问题之前停了下来。 如果你有多个程序访问存储，例如一个数据库（你正在对其做快照）和使用该数据库的应用程序，那么当您写入的数据库状态领先或落后于应用程序状态时，你就面临快照不一致的风险。 你需要一种机制来冻结快照之外的所有 I/O，以确保快照数据是有用的。

sents.en: Consistency groups.
sents.zh: 一致性组。

sents.en: The article kinda almost gets there, but stops right before it realizes there’s a problem.
sents.zh: 这篇文章差不多接近要点了，但就在意识到存在问题之前停了下来。

sents.en: If you have multiple programs accessing the storage, s.a. a database (that you are snapshotting) and the application using the database, then you are risking an inconsistent snapshot when the database state you wrote is ahead or behind the application state.
sents.zh: 如果你有多个程序访问存储，例如一个数据库（你正在对其做快照）和使用该数据库的应用程序，那么当您写入的数据库状态领先或落后于应用程序状态时，你就面临快照不一致的风险。

sents.en: You need a mechanism to freeze all I/O beside the snapshot in order to ensure that the snapshot data is useful.
sents.zh: 你需要一种机制来冻结快照之外的所有 I/O，以确保快照数据是有用的。

paragraphs.en: ACLs. And similar external mapping to the storage being used, eg. what if the users come from an LDAP server? Similar problem with symlinks coming from/going to ouitside the snapshot.
paragraphs.zh: 访问控制列表（ACL）。 以及类似的对所使用存储的外部映射，例如：如果用户来自 LDAP 服务器怎么办？ 来自/指向快照之外的符号链接也有类似的问题。

sents.en: ACLs.
sents.zh: 访问控制列表（ACL）。

sents.en: And similar external mapping to the storage being used, eg. what if the users come from an LDAP server?
sents.zh: 以及类似的对所使用存储的外部映射，例如：如果用户来自 LDAP 服务器怎么办？

sents.en: Similar problem with symlinks coming from/going to ouitside the snapshot.
sents.zh: 来自/指向快照之外的符号链接也有类似的问题。

paragraphs.en: Sparse file support. Let’s say you have a few VM images in your snapshot: if your tool doesn’t support sparse files, it will likely greatly inflate the image sizes.
paragraphs.zh: 支持稀疏文件。 假设你的快照中有几个虚拟机镜像：如果你的工具不支持稀疏文件，很可能会大幅增大镜像体积。

sents.en: Sparse file support.
sents.zh: 支持稀疏文件。

sents.en: Let’s say you have a few VM images in your snapshot: if your tool doesn’t support sparse files, it will likely greatly inflate the image sizes.
sents.zh: 假设你的快照中有几个虚拟机镜像：如果你的工具不支持稀疏文件，很可能会大幅增大镜像体积。

paragraphs.en: Bottom line, either use the product’s own snapshot functionality (ZFS has those), or switch to the product that does.
paragraphs.zh: 总之，要么使用该产品自带的快照功能（ZFS 就有这种功能），要么改用具备该功能的产品。
